document.title: Islamic Terrorists: Using Nongovernmental Organizations Extensively (CTC 99-40007)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified

organizations.name: Maktab al-Khidamat
organizations.notes: Pakistan-based NGO established in Peshawar in 1984 to facilitate travel and training of Arab volunteers fighting with the mujahidin in Afghanistan; the premier example of a private NGO used by terrorists; has opened offices in at least 20 countries since the mid-1980s.

organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Bin Ladin's organization; members planted in or coopted within NGOs.

organizations.name: al-Haramayn
organizations.notes: Gulf-based NGO; case study of Bin Ladin's diversion of resources through sympathetic employees in its offices.

organizations.name: United Nations High Commission for Refugees
organizations.notes: Accreditation of Islamic NGOs gives credentials that terrorists use to travel and establish cells.

places.name: Afghanistan

events.description: Maktab al-Khidamat (MAK) established in Peshawar by Usama Bin Ladin and Abdallah Azzam to facilitate travel and training of Arab volunteers.
CIA DCI Counterterrorist Center issues intelligence report on terrorist use of NGOs.
Founding of Maktab al-Khidamat (MAK) in Peshawar by Bin Ladin and Abdallah Azzam to facilitate Arab volunteers' travel and training for the Afghan jihad.
MAK opened new offices in at least 20 countries since the mid-1980s.
Outbreak of Balkans conflict in mid-1990s led Islamic activists to open Europe-based NGOs to aid Bosnian Muslims.
DCI Counterterrorist Center issued intelligence report on Islamic terrorists' use of NGOs.

key_claims: Only a few dozen of more than 6,000 Islamic NGOs support terrorists.
NGOs are exploited mainly at local branch offices by sympathetic employees, often without leadership knowledge.
NGO logistics support (cover employment, false documents, travel, training, sometimes weapons) is often more valuable to terrorists than funds.
Maktab al-Khidamat, founded in Peshawar in 1984 by Bin Ladin and Azzam, is the premier example of a private NGO supporting militants.
Bin Ladin diverted al-Haramayn resources via employees and created or planted al-Qa'ida members in NGOs.
Gulf state controls on fundraising have been largely ineffective because they do not address diversion at branch offices.
